messages:
auditor-jane: Hi team — auditor here. For the SOC2 scope: we need evidence linking RBAC changes to KMS key activity and any incident triage for the March rotation window. Specifically: chain-of-custody for the RBAC change, audit log excerpts showing key rotation or GenerateDataKey calls, and the mapping between service accounts, role bindings, and the KMS key IDs. Can you confirm what artifacts you can provide and an ETA?

amy-sec: Hi Jane — we can provide those. Quick clarifying q's: (1) what exact time range do you want for logs? (2) do you need raw CloudTrail events or a curated CSV + screenshots? (3) do you want the PR/approval trail for RBAC changes?

auditor-jane: Thanks Amy. Range: 2026-02-25T00:00:00Z to 2026-03-05T23:59:59Z (this covers the rotation/triage). Both raw CloudTrail/CSP logs and a short curated CSV would be ideal. Yes please include PR/approval trail for any rolebinding/service-account changes.

ben-eng: We'll collect: git history + PR diff for the RBAC changes, k8s audit snapshots (api-server audit logs), CloudTrail KMS events, and our SIEM correlation IDs for the incident. Ben here — I'll start assembling.

ben-eng: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1629 (rbac: limit access for secret-syncer)
ben-eng: Git diff (snippet):
```
- kind: RoleBinding
- metadata:
-   name: secret-syncer-prod
- subjects:
- - kind: ServiceAccount
-   name: secret-syncer
+ kind: RoleBinding
+ metadata:
+   name: secret-syncer-prod
+ subjects:
+ - kind: ServiceAccount
+   name: secret-syncer
+   namespace: infra
+ roleRef:
+   name: secrets-reader
```

amy-sec: KMS evidence note: we use AWS KMS envelope encryption. Key rotation for alias/rdw-prod-secrets occurred within window. Sample commands we ran to validate:
```
aws kms get-key-rotation-status --key-id alias/rdw-prod-secrets
# RotationEnabled: true

aws kms list-key-rotation-status --key-id 1234abcd-12ab-34cd-56ef-1234567890ab
```

amy-sec: Sample CloudTrail excerpt (sanitized):
```
{"eventTime":"2026-03-02T14:22:11Z","eventName":"EnableKeyRotation","userIdentity":{"arn":"arn:aws:iam::111222333444:user/infra-ops"},"requestParameters":{"keyId":"arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111222333444:key/1234abcd-12ab-34cd-56ef-1234567890ab"}}
{"eventTime":"2026-03-02T14:25:00Z","eventName":"GenerateDataKey","userIdentity":{"arn":"arn:aws:sts::111222333444:assumed-role/secret-syncer-role/session"},"requestParameters":{"keyId":"arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111222333444:key/1234abcd-12ab-34cd-56ef-1234567890ab"}}
```

amy-sec: Splunk query we used to extract KMS events:
```
index=redwood_cloudtrail sourcetype=aws:cloudtrail (eventName=EnableKeyRotation OR eventName=GenerateDataKey OR eventName=RotateKey)
| table _time, eventName, userIdentity.arn, requestParameters.keyId, eventSource
```

dave-sre: SIEM correlation IDs for the incident: CORR-20260302-0817 and CORR-20260302-0821. Those map to the CloudTrail events above and to the k8s audit events where the rolebinding change was applied. k8s audit sample:
```
{"kind":"RoleBinding","namespace":"infra","user":"system:serviceaccount:infra:infra-deploy","verb":"patch","timestamp":"2026-03-02T14:21:50Z","objectRef":{"name":"secret-syncer-prod"}}
```

deploy-bot: Deploy status: PR #1629 merged by @ben-eng at 2026-03-02T14:20:05Z. CI: all checks passed.

auditor-jane: Good — can you also provide chain-of-custody: who requested the RBAC change, approval thread, and a signed/dated evidence manifest? We need proof that the change was approved by a manager and tracked in our change control log.

amy-sec: Approval trail: internal changelog ticket CHG-879 (links to Slack convo): https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/CHG-879. Approver: @lina-product (product security reviewer) + @matt-sec (security manager). We'll export the ticket history and include the Slack thread transcript.

ameny-sec: We'll produce an evidence bundle with: CSV of CloudTrail events (filtered & redacted), k8s audit log slice, PR diff + signed approval screenshot, CHG ticket export, and an evidence manifest (MD5 checksums). ETA: end of day tomorrow (2026-03-05).

auditor-jane: That timeline works. One more: are ephemeral credentials used anywhere that would complicate key custody? For example, short-lived service tokens that bypass KMS logging?

dave-sre: We use STS-assumed roles for the secret-syncer, which show up in CloudTrail as assumed-role ARNs — GenerateDataKey calls are recorded. There is no route that bypasses KMS (no custom HSM outside AWS). Ephemeral creds are fine — they still appear in CloudTrail with principalId.

ben-eng: I'll attach a sample mapping CSV in the bundle showing: service-account -> role -> assumed-role ARN -> KMS keyId. Sample row: "infra/secret-syncer, secrets-reader, arn:aws:sts::111222333444:assumed-role/secret-syncer-role/session, arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111222333444:key/1234abcd-..."

amy-sec: For the manifest we'll include checksums and a short verification script. Example verification snippet for auditor:
```
sha256sum evidence-bundle.zip > evidence-bundle.sha256
curl -O <presigned-url>/evidence-bundle.zip
sha256sum -c evidence-bundle.sha256
```

auditor-jane: Perfect. Please add a note in the manifest about redaction: all user emails will be redacted to IDs, and any PII removed. Also include the KMS key policy excerpt showing that only infra-ops and the secrets-reader role can call GenerateDataKey.

amy-sec: Noted. We'll include key policy snippet and explicit mapping. I'll ping when the S3 presigned link is up.

ben-eng: Packaging now, will hand off to amy for upload.

dave-sre: Once uploaded I will file the SIEM evidence ticket with the correlation IDs and mark for auditor access.

auditor-jane: Thanks all — looking forward to the bundle. If anything else comes up I will follow up in this thread. :thumbsup:
